notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs the canonical C/D raw-supremum identity, actual positivity before limits, every-degree convergence and finite-generation implication. Rejudges normal-surface, exact BFJ, conductor, cusp, crossing and gluing arguments at their qualified scopes. All five actual FINAL notes and five distinct expanded proofs were read separately, together with fourteen complete immediate primary carriers and two formula images. Historical recursive audit remains qualified.
notes.text:
The sole mathematical input is ENTIRE qualified G331, including its mandatory annotation, source ledger and exact scope. Current 422/420 actual FINAL fields, assembled notes, distinct expanded proofs, source records, programs and compiler observations are DATA. The independently geometric classes C and D retain actual negative effective finite REAL Cartier presentations on directed ACTUAL primary blowups, nonnegative degree on EVERY contracted proper integral curve, quotient-support evaluations, uniform comparison with primary/unit profiles, actual decreasing nets and full-fibre positive descent. No envelope theorem, arbitrary-model cofinality or literal radial identity is imported.

Here is an independently reconstructed canonical lemma. For an excellent reduced local ring, primary gauge a, compact X=V_a and finite continuous signed obstacle f, define A_0=R and A_m={g:v(g)+m f(v)>=0 for every v in X}. Ultrametricity proves idealness; a sufficiently high power of a lies in A_m; and A_m A_n is contained in A_(m+n). If f is negative anywhere, A_m is proper primary; otherwise it is R. A monic integral-dependence equation has a uniquely least-valued leading term whenever finite v(g) violates its defining bound, proving integral closedness. Infinite values already satisfy the tests. The finite continuous profile h_m=-v(A_m)/m lies below f. Its ACTUAL primary blowup carries effective Cartier E_m, and -E_m/m is negative effective and relatively ample, with positive degree on EVERY contracted integral curve BEFORE a limit is identified. The unit case is zero.

The raw supremum p(f) over C minorants equals the supremum over D minorants and sup_m h_m. G331 gives uniform rational primary/unit approximation in C. Correcting an approximation by a small negative rational gauge constant retains the obstacle inequality and becomes ideal multiplication after synchronizing denominators. A rational competitor -v(I)/r<=f has I contained in A_r. Conversely h_m is itself a competitor. For g=inf_i g_i in D with g<=f, the directed open sets {g_i<f+epsilon} cover compact X. One common index works everywhere, and g_i-epsilon belongs to C and lies below f. Thus g<=p(f)+epsilon; let epsilon decrease. Partial bottom is included. The constant -max(0,-min f) supplies a finite lower barrier. Positivity or upper semicontinuity of p is not assumed.

Put M_1=||v(A_1)|| and H_N=max_(1<=r<=N)h_r. Writing m=kr+s with 0<=s<r, grading gives h_m>=(kr/m)h_r-s M_1/m>=h_r-r M_1/m. Hence H_N-N M_1/m<=h_m<=p. Every canonical degree converges pointwise to finite lower semicontinuous p. Compact increasing strict-test covers prove that p is continuous iff H_N converges uniformly, iff h_m converges uniformly. Then p belongs to C and is the greatest C/D minorant. Negative gauge shifts give ||p(f)-p(F)||<=||f-F||. Finite homogeneous generation implies continuity: homogeneous generators g_j of degrees d_j give inf_m v(A_m)/m=min_j v(g_j)/d_j by homogeneous monomial evaluation and pure powers. With L divisible by all d_j, p=-v(J)/L for J=(g_j^(L/d_j)). If f is negative somewhere J is proper, and it is unit at every nonmaximal prime because A_1 is; hence J is primary. Non-FG alone is not a CE counterexample.

Primary changes are exact. With d(v)=v(b)>0, T(v)=v/d(v), and f_b(Tv)=f_a(v)/d(v), every canonical inequality divides by the same bounded positive continuous factor. Canonical ideals are unchanged; profiles and raw envelopes divide by d. Order bijections preserve greatest-minorant existence. G331 completion transport and exact primary contraction preserve these statements on all supports. A decreasing family of continuous obstacles with C envelopes has a greatest D envelope given by their actual decreasing envelope net; no increasing completion or arbitrary net flattening is used.

The normal-surface theorem was independently rejudged at its exact domain. For EVERY excellent NORMAL local DOMAIN of dimension TWO, normalize the blowup of a finite product of primary ideals including a. This is a normal projective integral surface, regular off the closed fibre, with finite singular locus and normal singular local completions. These are exactly Stacks 54.14.5 condition (4). The complete immediate 54.14.3--5 proofs provide a finite regular refinement by normalized blowups. Complete-normal-surface resolution, rational/double-point steps, completion transfer and gluing remain disclosed deeper published dependencies.

Composition ampleness 29.38.7--8 combines negative tautological bundles into an ample O(-E), with E effective exceptional of full support. Normal proper birational 37.53.6 gives H0(Y,O)=R. This particular refinement is an ACTUAL primary blowup: finitely many affine nonvanishing section charts of powers of O(-E) cover Y; equalize degrees. Section localization in the complete 28.27.11 proof writes finite affine algebra generators as t/s_i^k. In a common higher degree, s_i^K and t s_i^(K-k) give projective ratios generating every affine chart, hence a closed immersion. The sections lie in R and generate invertible J O_Y, with J proper and unit off the marked point. The immersion factors into integral Bl_J and contains its dense punctured open; its defining ideal is zero. This proves the needed finite-list refinement, not arbitrary-model cofinality.

On regular Y, exceptional prime curves E_i are actual effective Cartier. Write E_a=sum a_i E_i with a_i>0, D=sum d_i E_i, and Q_ij=deg_(E_i)O(E_j), over the marked residue field. Off-diagonal entries are nonnegative and symmetric by local effective intersection lengths. Every contracted integral curve is one of the E_i. Feasible vectors satisfy z<=min(d,0), Qz>=0. A sufficiently negative -M a is feasible because O(-E_a) is generated. Coordinate maxima preserve feasibility: in each row keep one input's diagonal coordinate and increase its nonnegative off-diagonal terms. Compact coordinate maximization above the barrier yields a greatest z*. Every feasible vector joins the barrier inside this compact box. Thus Z*=sum z_i*E_i is actual negative effective REAL Cartier and curve-nef.

For any primary competitor -v(I)/s<=f_D, remove its exceptional divisorial part F_I. Normal height-one intersection puts every generator in H0(Y,O(-F_I)). On EACH exceptional CURVE some generator has nonzero generic restriction after removal, so its line-bundle degree is nonnegative. Therefore -F_I/s is feasible and <=Z*. For every support p, the valuation ring of Frac(R/p) has its proper centre on Y, with generic point off the fibre. Pull back the exceptional invertible lattice with its generic trivialization; regular generator ratios give -v(I)/s<=f_(-F_I/s)<=f_(Z*) even when generators are killed. The canonical lemma gives p(f_D)=f_(Z*). Signed primary differences form a separating lattice: min(vI-vJ,vK-vH)=v(IH+KJ)-v(JH), constants come from a, and (g)+a^N separates all supports. Compact lattice approximation and Lipschitz continuity prove CE for ALL continuous signed obstacles on these normal surfaces, over arbitrary residue fields and in equal or mixed characteristic. No general rate or finite generation follows.

The BFJ application remains ONLY at a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. For a signed model F fixed by a retraction, max-directed nef coefficients below F, with a negative barrier, have bounded weak-nef supremum W. BFJ 3.11 supplies substantive CLOSED-simplex continuity, and ALL-retraction infima define H_W on every semivaluation. Divisorial tests, simplex continuity and refining the fixed model give H_W<=F on every support. G331's exact BFJ D comparison bounds every competitor by H_W. Canonical ideals equal L-infinity(mW); truncating by (g)+mhat^N with N>=m max(0,-min F) passes divisorial tests to all supports, and G331 contracts primary ideals. If W is nonzero, 3.14 gives strict negativity and fixed-complex thinness gives A_thin<=-CW. The WHOLE 3.18 proof applies for real t>C; using t=m+C yields (1+C/m)W<=W_m<=W, hence 0<=H_W-h_m<=C max(0,-min F)/m on EVERY support through closed-simplex continuity and all-retraction infima. Uniform model density and Lipschitz give smooth CE at exactly these hypotheses. Zero uses the unit ideal, bottom is separate, and DVR/empty cases are direct. Higher-dimensional positive/mixed-characteristic source CE is not inferred.

If the FULL reduced conductor-quotient boundary restriction is injective, G331's finite singleton stratum and infinite quotient-fibre rule give a normalization boundary homeomorphism and positive order/isometric C/D transport. Envelopes transport and CE is equivalent on the normal centres. Primary conductors suffice. Finite radicial reduced quotient maps also suffice: every support has its unique support prime and purely inseparable quotient field extension, forcing w(t)=v(t^(p^e))/p^e. No perfection or common exponent is required. Canonical ideals contract; extension equality or inherited rates are not asserted.

The retained cusp arguments were checked. A numerical-semigroup ring k[t^H,z]_0 has normalization k[t,z]_0 and conductor t^c S: a coefficient at exponent h<c cannot be conductor because multiplying by t^(c-1-h) exposes the forbidden exponent c-1. Localization preserves the finite-module conductor. Reduced quotients are the identical z-ring, so transport gives CE in the exact BFJ range in every dimension and on surfaces over every field; the mixed cusp over Z_p has the same normal-surface transport. For H=<2,3>, b=z_1+t and A=w((b,t^2,z_2,...)), the actual primary K_m=(b^m(z_1-mt),t^2b^m,t^(2m+2))+(z_2,...)^m has no t-linear term in any characteristic. With s=w(t),u=w(z_1),B=w(b),U=min_(j>=2)w(z_j), normalization min(2s,u,U)=1 and A=min(B,2s,U), all generators have value>=mA. If U=A there is equality. Otherwise 2s<=B forces s=u=1 and the last generator gives mA+2; B<2s and s<=u gives s<=1 and the second gives mA+2s; s>u gives B=w(z_1-mt)=u=1 and the first gives mA+1 even when m=0 in k. Thus the all-support error is <=2/m. In characteristic zero, the conductor valuation and monomial (t,b) weights (1,2) give A=1,2. A primary generator attaining z-order e has no t-linear term, so its degree-e part cannot be a scalar b^e. After z=b-t, some t^(e-j)b^j with j<e survives, of weight<=2e-1; other total degrees cannot cancel it. Every nonzero finite REAL positive primary combination retains strict ratio<2, while A has ratio2. This proves CE without raw attainment or FG, not CE failure.

The threefold example remains diagnostic: blow up the regular origin and two rational exceptional points P,Q. For I=(z)+m^2, the x-chart is x(w,x), so its divisorial part is E_1+2E_2+2E_3. Its negative restriction on E_1=Bl_(P,Q)P^2 is H-e_P-e_Q; the joining line has degree -1, while the other exceptional planes have degree1. The same ample-section/Rees argument makes this model actual primary. A generic section on an exceptional SURFACE does not imply all-curve-nefness. The genuine primary profile stays geometric on its own blowup. This is not normal CE failure.

For the inherited crossings, direct component factorization and ordinary-order comparison bound every second-branch competitor by its generic order value. For 0<a<b, the compatible obstacle -a on branch1 and -a-(b-a)/w(y) on branch2 has canonical ideal m^ceil(mb)+x m^(ceil(ma)-1), raw p=-a at finite-x first-branch points and -b elsewhere, and exact gap ceil(mb)/m-a. The signed model (1/2)v((y)+m^2)-(3/2)v(m) has the same half-gap filtration. Actual negative primary divisors are ample before limits. Monomial x=r,z_j=1 approaches the conductor and proves non-USC, no greatest C/D minorant, and failure of positivity of USC regularization. Perturbation <1/4 preserves the half-gap contradiction. These are checked inherited deductions, not new progress.

For regular normal SURFACE centres glued along the SAME marked DVR with principal nonzero kernels and common quotient gauge, normal CE gives H_i. Set a=min H_i(o_i). Zero dichotomy gives all H_i=0 if a=0; otherwise scaling negative H_i, and constant a on zero branches, gives C barriers B_i<=H_i with B_i(o_i)=a. For N>=n||H_i-B_i||, max(B_i,H_i-w(x_i)/n)=max(B_i,H_i-w((x_i)+a_i^N)/n) is C and equals a at o_i. Actual primary truncation and full-fibre positive descent give target minorants reaching H_i off the conductor. Therefore raw p equals H_i there and a at the shared point; equality of all H_i(o_i) is necessary and sufficient for greatest C/D existence. Unequal values contradict USC along a finite-kernel-value dense NET.

The inherited cross-component necessity can be checked directly. With regular conductor c_0 and normalization idempotents e_1,e_2, j=c_0e_1 and ell=c_0e_2 are actual downstairs elements. At a cross-component fibre alpha,beta, the normal bound gives g(beta)<=g(nu)/K. Choose L>nu(ell) and B with D_0=1+B(1-nu(ell)/L)>K. The obstacle (B/L)v((ell)+a^L)-(B+1) is -1 on component1, while every minorant has common-fibre value <=-D_0/K<-1. Actual primary a^((B+1)n)+(j)a^n reaches -1 on the dense finite-j first-component locus and equals -(B+1) elsewhere, contradicting USC of a greatest minorant. A valuation of a positive-dimensional R/(p_1+p_2) lifts into both normalization components and supplies such a fibre. Consequently excellent reduced local dimension<=2 with NORMAL component rings has universal CE exactly when every pairwise intersection is zero-dimensional: sufficiency follows from uniqueness of the component at each support below m and normal-surface/DVR transport. This does not classify irreducible nonnormal rings.

Reduced curve links have DVR normalization centres and finite conductor values, so no conductor boundary identifications occur. Positive descent gives all nonpositive branch functions and envelope min(f,0). Literal classical/CLD logarithmic radial extension remains distinct, preserving its mixed-zero obstruction. Nilpotents are invisible and dimension-zero reduction has empty boundary. Products, energy and full finite operators remain separate.

notes.detailedSummary: Proves the CRT/conductor proposal on every support with actual signed primary-model obstacles and all-curve-positive primary competitors. Requires a full fibre joining distinct closed normal centres, not distinct minimal components. Gives a positive canonical uniform gap in every degree and quantified perturbation stability. Same-centre fibres are not decided.
notes.text:
Use ENTIRE qualified G331 and n1. Let R be excellent reduced local of positive dimension, a a proper primary gauge, S its finite normalization, and rho its FULL normalized boundary quotient. Let M_1,...,M_q be the finitely many closed normalization centres over m, and S_i their normal local domains. If a rho-fibre contains alpha at M_1 and beta at a DISTINCT M_2, then a bounded strictly negative continuous signed PRIMARY-MODEL obstacle has neither a greatest geometric C nor a greatest geometric D minorant. S may be a DOMAIN. No source CE or higher-dimensional resolution is assumed.

Choose r_i>=1 with M_i^r_i contained in a_i=aS_i. Every normalized source w at that centre has w(M_i)>=1/r_i. Localization denominators outside M_i have value0, so w(a)=w(a_i)=1 on ALL supports. Chinese remainder gives h in S equal to1 modulo M_1 and0 modulo EVERY other marked maximal ideal, and k in S equal to0 modulo M_1 and1 modulo M_2. Thus h is a unit at M_1 and a nonunit at every other centre; k is a unit at M_2. These are actual semilocal normalization elements, not downstairs units or unavailable domain idempotents.

Choose a regular conductor element c_0. Since the conductor is an S-ideal, c_0 times EVERY S-element belongs to R. The nontrivial fibre is conductor-infinite by G331, so alpha and beta kill c_0. The conductor is proper; c_0 is a nonunit of R, positive and nonzero on generic centred source valuations. Choose a normalized centred divisorial nu at M_2 by G331 density. The normal-domain bound gives finite K>=1 with nu(I)<=K beta(I) for every unit-or-primary ideal of S_2. Explicitly nu(f)<=C_nu ord_(M_2)(f) for nonzero nonunits, while beta(M_2)>=1/r_2. A generator attaining the primary ideal's finite beta-value gives nu(I)<=C_nu r_2 beta(I); units are zero. Negative REAL combinations, uniform comparison and actual decreasing infima therefore give g(rho beta)<=g(rho nu)/K for EVERY target geometric C/D function, including bottom. The bound is applied only to excellent NORMAL S_2, not nonnormal R.

Put d=nu(c_0)>0. Choose integers L>d and B>0 with D_0=1+B(1-d/L)>K; set b=B+1. Choose M>=L r_1 and ell=c_0 k^M in R. On EVERY M_1 source support, w(ell)>=M/r_1>=L, while nu(ell)=d because k is a unit at M_2. The actual ideal I=(ell)+a^L is proper primary: it contains a^L, and ell cannot be a downstairs unit since its M_1 value is positive. Define F=(B/L)v(I)-b v(a). On V_a it lies in [-b,-1], equals -1 on the ENTIRE M_1 boundary image and at the common fibre, and F(rho nu)=-D_0<-K. Primary evaluations prove continuity on every support. F is a signed exceptional REAL Cartier evaluation on a directed common ACTUAL primary blowup of I and a.

For each n>=1 choose M_n>=B n max_(i!=1)r_i, put j_n=c_0 h^(M_n) in R, T_n=a^(bn)+(j_n)a^n, and q_n=-v(T_n)/n. T_n is actual proper primary. Its negative effective divisor -E_(T_n)/n is relatively ample on its ACTUAL blowup and has positive degree on EVERY contracted integral curve BEFORE a limit. On M_1 its exact profile is max(-b,-1-w(c_0)/n); at every other centre w(j_n)>=M_n/r_i>=Bn, hence q_n=-b. Infinite values and nonminimal supports are included. Thus q_n<=F EVERYWHERE. On the M_1 finite-c_0 locus, sup_n q_n=-1. That locus is dense: c_0 is nonzero in S_1 and every generic-support centred divisorial valuation has finite c_0-value. In particular alpha is in its closure. A NET suffices; no metrizability is assumed.

Every geometric minorant g<=F has g(rho beta)<=-D_0/K<-1. A greatest minorant would dominate every q_n and equal -1 on the dense finite-c_0 M_1 locus because F=-1 there. Its normalization pullback is USC. A strict sublevel neighbourhood of alpha at its forced value below -1 would meet that dense locus, a contradiction. Thus neither greatest C nor greatest D minorant exists. The raw supremum p equals -1 on this dense locus and is <=-D_0/K at the common point, so p is not USC. This establishes the proposed CRT route with exact ring membership, uniform centre bounds and actual geometric positivity.

Set eta=D_0/K-1>0. Each canonical h_m from n1 is continuous and <=p. At alpha, h_m<=-D_0/K. Along a finite-c_0 M_1 net approaching alpha, h_m converges to this value while p=-1. Consequently ||p-h_m||>=eta in EVERY degree. The canonical algebra is not finitely generated by n1's proved implication. No complete formula for p elsewhere is asserted. Failure is stable for ||F'-F||<epsilon<(D_0-K)/(K+1): q_n-epsilon are C minorants, forcing any greatest minorant to be >=-1-epsilon on the dense locus, whereas the normal bound forces common-fibre value <=(-D_0+epsilon)/K<-1-epsilon. Homogeneous primary transport divides by the same bounded positive denominator and preserves nonexistence and canonical ideals.

An algebraic sufficient condition is a conductor-quotient boundary fibre lifting into distinct marked centres. Positive-dimensional intersections of distinct minimal components supply one by lifting a valuation of R/(p_1+p_2) through both finite normalizations. This recovers the earlier crossing theorem as a special case. Universal CE therefore requires EVERY normalization fibre to stay within ONE marked centre. It does not require, by this argument, that such a fibre be singleton. Several normalization centres alone are insufficient without a connecting full fibre. Reduced curves remain consistent because their conductor quotient boundary is empty.

Same-centre fibres, general NORMAL dimension>=3 CE, products, energy and full finite operators are not solved. Every G331 model/source/audit/radial qualification remains attached. Artifacts n2.md and n2.tex contain the proof. Rerun: python assemble.py; python verify_delivery.py. Finite arithmetic is diagnostic, not theorem certification.

notes.detailedSummary: Proves domain normalization, exact conductor/quotients, signed primary obstacle, complete raw envelope and every-degree canonical ideals over characteristic-not-two fields in every dimension at least two, and excellent DVR surfaces with two invertible. Every competitor has actual ample primary positivity before limits. This is a nonnormal failure, not a normal CE counterexample.
notes.text:
Use ENTIRE qualified G331 and n1--n2. For ANY field k with char(k)!=2 and d>=2, let z=(z_1,...,z_(d-1)) and R=k[u,v,z]_(u,v,z)/(v^2-u^2(1+u)), m=(u,v,z). This is an excellent DOMAIN of dimension d: 1+u is not a square in k(u,z), since its prime divisor has odd order, so the quadratic is irreducible. Its parametrization is u=t^2-1, v=t(t^2-1). The normal polynomial ring S_0=k[t,z] is finite over unlocalized R_0 via integral t satisfying t^2=1+u, and has the same fraction field because t=v/u. It is the normalization. Localizing by R_0\m gives a NORMAL DOMAIN S with exactly two centres M_+=(t-1,z), M_-=(t+1,z). It equals the semilocalization of k[t,z] at those centres: an element outside their union is a unit in the finite algebra over local R. S is not a product.

The conductor is exact. With A=k[u,z], S_0=A direct-sum tA and R_0=A direct-sum tuA. Membership of a+t b in R_0 requires b divisible by u; multiplication by t additionally requires a divisible by u. Conversely uS_0 multiplies S_0 into R_0. Thus the conductor is uS_0 before localization and uS afterwards, by localization of the annihilator of finite S_0/R_0. As an R-ideal it is (u,v). Its quotients are R/c=k[z]_(z) and S/c=TWO copies of that ring, using coprime factors t-1,t+1. Exactly R=k[z]_(z)+uS, by subtracting the lifted quotient residue. This is a conductor fibre product, not a decomposition of the normalization domain. Moreover mS=(u,z), which is the maximal ideal on each normal local centre because the opposite sign factor is a unit.

Every finite-u target boundary point has its unique source lift. At infinite u-value, EVERY quotient-boundary semivaluation on k[z] has two lifts, one on each centre, and precisely these are identified by G331. For d=2 the conductor boundary is one point o with z_1=1; in higher dimension every quotient support remains. This proves the marked-centre hypothesis of n2 for an irreducible germ.

There is an explicit obstacle independent of an unknown Izumi constant. Let ell=v-u=u(t-1), I=(ell)+m^2 and F=(1/2)v(I)-2v(m). This is a continuous signed ACTUAL primary-model evaluation. At the plus centre put s=w(t-1), Z=min_j w(z_j); min(s,Z)=1 and w(u)=s, while t+1 is a unit. Hence w(ell)=2s>=2 and F=-1 on the ENTIRE plus boundary. At the minus centre put r=w(t+1); min(r,Z)=1, t-1 is a unit and w(ell)=r. Thus F=(1/2)min(r,2)-2, in [-3/2,-1]. Every conductor value is -1. Infinite coordinates are included; I is proper primary.

The generic ordinary-order valuation nu_- of the regular minus centre has r=Z=1 and F=-3/2. Every normalized semivaluation on that centre dominates ordinary order: all regular parameters have value>=1, elements of the e-th maximal power have value>=e, and units have value0. Hence w(J)>=nu_-(J) for every target unit-or-primary ideal. Negative REAL combinations, G331 uniform comparison and actual decreasing infima give g(rho w)<=g(rho nu_-) for EVERY target geometric C/D function on the entire minus image, including conductor supports. All minorants of F are therefore <=-3/2 there.

For n>=1 let j_n=u(t+1)^(n-1), an ACTUAL R-element by the conductor, T_n=m^(3n)+(j_n)m^(2n), and q_n=-v(T_n)/(2n). On the plus centre, q_n=max(-3/2,-1-s/(2n)); on the minus centre, w(j_n)=nr>=n and q_n=-3/2. These are <=F on every source/target support. Their negative effective primary divisors -E_(T_n)/(2n) are relatively ample and positive on EVERY contracted integral curve before limits. The constant -3/2 is also a competitor. Therefore the COMPLETE raw C/D supremum is p=-1 on the plus-centre finite-u locus and p=-3/2 on the entire minus image, including every conductor point.

At the plus centre, monomial w_R(t-1)=R and w_R(z_j)=1 converge pointwise as R->infinity to the valuation killing t-1 with ordinary z-order. Every fixed local unit denominator has value0. Target restrictions converge to a conductor point where p drops by1/2. Thus p is not USC and no greatest C or D minorant exists. This is NONNORMAL failure on an irreducible germ, not normal CE failure. Its USC regularization has value -1 at that conductor point and -3/2 at nu_-: the open test v(ell)<2 near nu_- meets only the minus image. These values violate g(o)<=g(nu_-), so regularization does not restore geometric positivity.

The canonical ideals are explicit in EVERY degree. Put c_m=ceil(3m/2) and, in S, J_m=(t-1,z)^(m-1)(t+1,z)^(c_m-1). The two semilocal ideals are comaximal because2 is invertible, so their product equals their intersection. Then A_m(F)=(z)^(c_m)R+uJ_m. This is a genuine R-ideal. Explicit finite generators are the z-monomials of total degree c_m and u t^epsilon times every product of a degree-(m-1) monomial in (t-1,z) and a degree-(c_m-1) monomial in (t+1,z), for epsilon=0,1. S=R+Rt, so these generate uJ_m over R. They are actual downstairs polynomials; use t^2=1+u and ut=v to express them in u,v,z.

Proof: ordinary-order tests at the plus/minus centres force respectively order>=m and order>=c_m. These suffice on EVERY source support by domination of ordinary order and F=-1 or F>=-3/2. Write f=g(z)+u a, with g in the local z-ring and a in S. The minus order condition forces g in (z)^(c_m), by reduction modulo the regular parameter u. Subtract the residue lift. Since u is a regular parameter at BOTH centres, the remaining u a has the required orders exactly when a lies in the (m-1)-st plus power and (c_m-1)-st minus power after localization. In the semilocal ring these are the intersection J_m. The converse is immediate. This includes localized denominators and cancellation and proves the ideal identity rather than inferring it from samples.

Localization at the plus centre makes the other centre's power unit. Hence on EVERY plus support, h_m=-min(c_m Z,s+m-1)/m. On every minus support and conductor point, h_m=-c_m/m. Every h_m has actual negative effective ample primary positivity from n1. These formulas prove pointwise convergence to p in EVERY degree. The EXACT uniform error is ||p-h_m||=c_m/m-1>=1/2: on the plus finite-u locus it is at most this number and is attained at Z=1 and finite s>=c_m-m+1; on the minus image the gap is c_m/m-3/2. Thus even degrees have error1/2, odd degrees have error1/2+1/(2m). The canonical algebra is not finitely generated by n1. Uniform perturbations <1/4 preserve failure using q_n-epsilon and the same ordinary-order inequality.

The proof already works in every field dimension d>=2 with char(k)!=2. notes.text:
Use ENTIRE qualified G331 and n1--n3. These deductions do not assert that every nonsingleton normalization fibre obstructs envelopes.

For the self-crossing SURFACE of n3 over any field of characteristic different from2, or its excellent DVR version with2 invertible, EVERY finite continuous signed obstacle f has an exact criterion. Its normalization S is a semilocal DOMAIN with two regular normal SURFACE centres. The boundary is their disjoint union and the C/D classes are their products by G331; disconnected boundary pieces do not require algebraic idempotents in S. Let H_+,H_- be the continuous geometric envelopes of the pulled-back obstacles, existing by n1's normal-surface theorem. The conductor quotient is the marked DVR k[z]_(z), or V, so the sole nontrivial boundary fibre is o_+,o_- over o. Set a=min(H_+(o_+),H_-(o_-)). Then the COMPLETE raw target C/D supremum equals H_i(w) when w(u)<infinity on centre i, and equals a at o. A greatest geometric C or D minorant exists iff H_+(o_+)=H_-(o_-); when it exists it is continuous and belongs to C.

For the positive lower bound, do not assume fibrewise minima are psh. If a=0, G331's normal zero dichotomy gives both H_i=0 and zero descends. If a<0 and H_i(o_i)<0, set B_i=(a/H_i(o_i))H_i, whose ratio is>=1 and B_i<=H_i. If H_i(o_i)=0, then H_i=0 and use constant B_i=a. These are C functions with B_i(o_i)=a. For n>=1 and integer N>=max(1,n||H_i-B_i||), define G_(i,n)=max(B_i,H_i-w(u)/n), interpreting the second term as bottom when u is killed. Exactly G_(i,n)=max(B_i,H_i-w((u)+a_i^N)/n), because H_i-N/n<=B_i. The ideal term has ACTUAL negative effective relatively ample primary positivity on EVERY contracted curve; G331 addition, scaling and maxima prove G_(i,n) belongs to C. The tuple has common conductor value a and is constant on EVERY fibre. Full-fibre POSITIVE descent gives a target C minorant. These minorants reach H_i at finite-u points and retain a at o; no increasing-limit closure is used. Every target D competitor pulls back below H_i and has common value<=both H_i(o_i), proving the upper bound.

If the conductor values agree, H_i itself descends to the continuous greatest envelope. If H_i(o_i)>a for one centre, finite-u points are dense by divisorial density and continuity of H_i gives a net to o_i with limiting raw value H_i(o_i)>p(o). Thus p is not USC and no greatest C/D minorant exists. This proof also applies to excellent reduced local surfaces with regular normal SURFACE centres, FULL infinite-conductor boundary consisting of one lift per centre over a single target point, and a nonzero conductor element u whose killed locus at each centre is just that point. These full-fibre/local-cone hypotheses are retained; no arbitrary conductor-minimum theorem is claimed.

Now compute the pinch family independently. For ANY field k let R=k[t^2,ty,y,s]_(t^2,ty,y,s) and S=k[t,y,s]_(t,y,s). R is a DOMAIN with presentation k[u,x,y,s]_(u,x,y,s)/(x^2-u y^2), u=t^2,x=ty. The quadratic is irreducible because u is not a square in k(u,y,s), including characteristic2; the subring embedding and rank-two normal form also prove the presentation. Integral t satisfies t^2=u and equals x/y in the fraction field. Thus S is finite, normal and birational, hence the normalization. Its UNIQUE marked centre is the origin because t^2,y,s vanish only there above the target maximal ideal.

With A=k[u,y,s], S_0=A direct-sum tA and R_0=A direct-sum tyA. Membership of a+tb in R_0 requires b divisible by y; multiplication by t additionally requires a divisible by y. Hence the conductor is exactly yS, whose target ideal is (y,x); the finite-module annihilator calculation localizes. Its quotient map is k[u,s]_(u,s)->k[t,s]_(t,s), u->t^2. The target maximal primary gauge (u,x,y,s) extends to (t^2,y,s). Every source and quotient support remains.

For char(k)!=2 there is an EXACT two-point FULL boundary fibre within this ONE marked normal centre. Let alpha have support (y,t-s), beta support (y,t+s), and give s value1 in their k[s] quotients. Both normalize the extended gauge by min(2,infinity,1)=1. Both kill the conductor and restrict to the target support (x,y,u-s^2), with u-value2 and s-value1. Their restrictions agree on EVERY R-element because x,y vanish and t^2=s^2 in both quotients; local units have value0. They differ because alpha(t-s)=infinity while beta(t-s)=1. There are exactly two lifts: modulo that target support, t^2=s^2 has exactly the primes t=+s and t=-s; their quotient fraction fields are k(s), on which the given base valuation has its unique identical extension. Both marked centres are still (t,y,s). This is a concrete same-centre residual, not an instance of n2.

Without s, the pinch SURFACE k[t^2,ty,y]_(t^2,ty,y) has conductor yS and quotient map k[u]_(u)->k[t]_(t). Each quotient centred boundary is a singleton. G331 finite-conductor uniqueness therefore makes normalization restriction bijective on the FULL boundary. At the conductor point the source has w(t)=1/2,w(y)=infinity for gauge (t^2,y), giving target u-value1. Positive order/isometric transport and n1's arbitrary-field normal-SURFACE CE prove continuous geometric envelopes for ALL continuous signed obstacles on this irreducible nonnormal pinch surface over EVERY field. The conductor is nonprimary. In characteristic different from2 the conductor quotient is separable degree two and is not falsely called radicial.

In characteristic2, the threefold quotient k[u,s]->k[t,s] is finite radicial. Every polynomial in t,s has its square in k[u,s] without k being perfect, so its value is forced to be half the value of that square; the same holds for quotient fields and every support. Thus the FULL normalization boundary map is bijective. CE is equivalent to normal-source CE, without a new arbitrary-characteristic threefold CE conclusion. The characteristic-not-two two-point fibre is not asserted in characteristic2.

There is a quantitative same-centre obstruction to the proposed METHOD, distinct from an envelope counterexample. On ANY excellent NORMAL local centre A with primary gauge a, choose normalized centred divisorial nu. G331 supplies K_nu>=1, independent of w, with nu(I)<=K_nu w(I) for every unit-or-primary ideal and EVERY normalized w on that SAME centre. Indeed nu(f)<=C ord_m(f), m^r contained in a and w(m)>=1/r give K_nu=C r after normalization; units are zero. Therefore every geometric C/D function satisfies g(w)<=g(nu)/K_nu throughout that centre. If F(nu)=-D with D>K_nu, EVERY minorant and its raw supremum are <=-D/K_nu<-1 EVERYWHERE. Competitors cannot approach -1 even on a dense subset there.

More concretely, if proposed separators j_n satisfy nu(j_n)>=c n, the element order bound gives w(j_n)/n>=c/K_nu for EVERY w. Thus max(-b,-1-w(j_n)/n)<=max(-b,-1-c/K_nu)<-1 when b>1. Powers of a nonunit cannot be shallow on one region and uniformly deep at a fixed divisorial point in the same marked centre. A local element is a unit at all centred valuations or a nonunit at all; CRT units cannot separate those lifts. This proves why n2's separate-centre argument cannot simply be reused at the pinch threefold's alpha,beta.

A general NORMAL/higher-dimensional deduction follows without CE. If finite continuous f on an excellent normal local domain is negative anywhere, continuity and divisorial density give centred divisorial nu with f(nu)<0. The uniform bound gives -max(0,-min f)<=p(f)(w)<=f(nu)/K_nu<0 on EVERY support. If f>=0, p(f)=0. Therefore the raw supremum has uniform strict negativity in the nonzero case. The same conclusion holds for an excellent nonnormal germ whose finite normalization has a SINGLE marked normal local centre, by pulling back f and all competitors. This includes the pinch test. It proves boundedness and excludes mixed-zero raw patterns; it does not establish USC, continuity, D attainment or greatest-minorant existence.

Finally, when source continuous envelopes are known and a particular pulled-back obstacle's source envelope is constant on EVERY normalization fibre, G331 positive descent gives a continuous target envelope: every target competitor pulls back below it and its compatible descent is a competitor. This is sufficient in the pinch threefold with smooth algebraically closed characteristic-zero source using n1's exact BFJ CE. Necessity is not asserted there. Same-centre nonsingleton-fibre classification and general excellent NORMAL dimension>=3 CE or qualifying failure remain OPEN. Products, energy, full finite operators and literal radial identification remain separate. Artifacts n4.md and n4.tex. Rerun: python assemble.py; python verify_delivery.py. Structural and coercivity claims are proofs relative to G331; finite arithmetic does not settle the residual envelope problem.
